_note: WINDOWS form (macOS/Linux users: use session_start_hook.macos.json instead; Git Bash users stay with THIS file and a C:\... path, not /c/... -- the hook runs outside your shell). Session-start priming: Claude Code injects this script's stdout as context before the first turn (memory highlights, active project, open tickets; read-only, fast-exit, never blocks a session). Merge the hooks block into your Claude Code settings file (user-wide: ~/.claude/settings.json; per-project: .claude/settings.json) -- back the file up first, and if it already has a hooks or SessionStart key, ADD this entry to the existing list instead of replacing it. Replace <ATLAS_PLUS_DIR> with the absolute path of your sextant clone (in PowerShell, `$PWD.Path` inside the clone). The interpreter must be the venv that has sextant installed; if that venv lives outside the clone, put its python path there instead of the placeholder path. Keep the double quotes around the interpreter path -- a profile path with a space in it splits the command without them. Do not copy this _note key into your settings. EASIER: `sextant setup` prints this block already filled in for your install (interpreter path, JSON escaping, ATLAS_* variables); a pipx/uv-tool install has no deploy/ folder and uses that command instead. If you fill it by hand on Windows, double every backslash inside the JSON string (C:\\sextant\\...) or the file will not parse.
